mappings.evidence_note: Pearson two-year scheme of work, issue 3: explicitly headed Year 1 AS content and Year 2 remaining A level content, cross-checked with bold common-AS content in specification Issue 4. This is a suggested standalone teaching sequence, not an exam-entry restriction. References in older SOW use some AS numbering; mapping follows the named skill and Issue 4 code. Overlapping scopes remain partial.

coverage.note: Expanding, factorising, algebraic division and factor theorem.
Polynomial/reciprocal graphs, intersections and proportion.
Translations and stretches of the Year 1 function repertoire.
Binomial expansion for positive integer powers.
Sine/cosine rules, triangle area and angles in degrees.
Trigonometric functions, exact values and graphs in degrees.
tan θ = sin θ/cos θ and sin²θ + cos²θ = 1.
Trigonometric equations in degrees using Year 1 functions.
Gradient/rate interpretation, polynomial first principles and second derivatives.
Differentiation of powers and polynomial expressions.
Gradients, tangents, normals, stationary points, monotonicity and modelling.
Integrating powers, polynomial expressions and finding a curve from its derivative.
Definite integrals and areas under polynomial curves and bounded by lines.
Two-dimensional vectors.
Magnitude/direction of vectors in two dimensions.
Vector operations and geometrical interpretation in two dimensions.
Position vectors/distances in two dimensions.
Two-dimensional geometry and vector modelling.
Scatter diagrams, linear regression, interpolation and qualitative correlation.
Independent/mutually exclusive events and basic discrete probability.
Language of hypothesis testing through the binomial model.
Fundamental SI units and derived velocity, acceleration, force and weight.
Constant acceleration in a straight line using scalar quantities.
Calculus for variable acceleration in a straight line.
Newton’s second law with parallel/perpendicular or supplied 2-D vector forces.
Newton’s third law, connected particles and simple equilibrium.
Further rational-expression manipulation.
Modulus graphs and additional function contexts.
Combined transformations and the extended A level function repertoire.
Expansion for rational powers, validity and approximation.
Radian measure, arc length and sector area.
Radian-measure expressions and the extended function repertoire.
Secant/cosecant/cotangent identities.
Radian-measure problems and equations using the extended A level repertoire.
First principles for sin/cos and convexity/concavity/inflections.
Exponential, logarithmic and trigonometric differentiation.
Inflection points and applications with the extended function repertoire.
Exponential, reciprocal and trigonometric integrals.
Further curve-to-curve and parametrically defined areas.
Three-dimensional vectors.
Three-dimensional vector magnitudes/directions.
Vector operations in three dimensions.
Position vectors/distances in three dimensions.
Three-dimensional geometry and further contexts.
Change of variable and exponential-model regression.
Use with conditional and continuous probability contexts.
Correlation coefficients and tests for zero correlation.
Moment as a derived quantity/unit.
Constant acceleration in two dimensions using vectors.
Two-dimensional vector calculus in kinematics.
Resolving forces at other angles and inclined-plane problems.
Resolving forces in two dimensions and coplanar equilibrium.

Translations and stretches of Year 1 functions.
Algebraic fractions, division and factor theorem; expanding/factorising also occurs in chapter 1.
Positive integer powers, factorial notation and binomial estimation; rational powers occur in Year 2.
Triangle ratios/rules/area in degrees; radian content is Year 2.
Graphs and transformations in degrees.
Exact values in degrees.
Year 1 sine/cosine/tangent identities.
Trigonometric equations using the Year 1 functions in degrees.

mappings.evidence_note: AS specification, "Progression from Advanced Subsidiary GCE to Advanced GCE": students "would have covered Topics 1-4 which are common to both qualifications but the additional topics 5-8 will need to be covered". Topics 1–4 are therefore Year 12 content and 5–8 Year 13. Core practicals follow the topic they are printed in.
